title: Synth-Pop
tagline: Pop songwriting reframed through electronic instruments.
summary: Synth-pop places synthesizers and electronic production at the center of accessible songcraft. Early artists explored affordable keyboards and studio technology, pairing new timbres with vocals, hooks, and familiar pop structures. The sound became especially visible in the late 1970s and 1980s, then returned in many forms. Its legacy reaches from chart pop to independent electronic scenes.

pillars.name: Kraftwerk
pillars.why: Kraftwerk's precise electronic arrangements helped establish a lasting vocabulary for pop made with machines.

pillars.name: Depeche Mode
pillars.why: Depeche Mode developed synth-pop into a durable band sound with dark textures and strong melodies.

pillars.name: Gary Numan
pillars.why: Numan brought stark synthesizer-led songwriting into the British pop mainstream.
